title: The music that made Dolly Parton a global icon
summary: From Appalachian mountain music to bluegrass and gospel hymns, Dolly Parton was no ordinary country singer.
author: Gemma Ware, Head of Audio, The Conversation UK, The Conversation
paragraphs: It was 1967, and country musician Porter Wagoner was introducing a guest on his weekly TV show.
The camera cuts to a woman with big, blonde beehive, wearing a magenta mini dress with the same shade of lipstick to match. It was in that moment a star was born.
Her name was Dolly Parton. In the following decades after that performance, Parton went on to become the “Queen of Country”.
But as musicologist and professor of music at Hamilton College in the US, Lydia Hamessley told The Conversation Weekly podcast, Parton’s music drew inspiration from across the board.
I heard so many resonances in her music of old-timey Appalachian or mountain music.
Her expressive way of singing felt like she had grown up hearing people singing in a particular way, that had such a heart to it and such a power to her voice.
Hamessley, who wrote a book on Parton’s songs and interviewed her as part of the research, said Parton’s real gift rested in her ability to tell a story.
[Dolly told me] she thinks of her songwriting as her workshop, and I was really intrigued by that idea.

She’s very instinctual as a songwriter. She sparks ideas, a turn of phrase, a little snippet of a melody. And then, “Oh, what can I do with that?”. She’ll work around it and everything. She can come up with the song, but then she’s not done.
I think of her as an artisan as well as an artist.
